title: Check yourself: the TransactionManager in depth

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A gift-card server journals to a Berkeley DB space. Its chain is RedeemCard (joins, and tells the card service to settle the redemption in commit), then SendResponse, then Audit (joins, writes a line in commit). The process dies inside Audit's commit of transaction 77, after the approval has gone out. What happens to transaction 77 at the next start?

options.text: It is committed again from the first participant, so RedeemCard tells the card service to settle a second time
options.says: the journal holds the state COMMITTING, not which commits already ran, so recovery commits every participant again

options.text: It is committed again from Audit onwards, so only the commit that was cut short is repeated
options.says: the journal records no progress inside the commit phase; recovery starts from the first participant

options.text: It is aborted on every participant, since the process died before the transaction was marked done
options.says: only a transaction left in PREPARING is aborted; one in COMMITTING had its outcome decided and is committed

options.text: It is aborted on the joined participants, since recovery cannot tell whether the approval reached the terminal
options.says: recovery decides by the journal's state, COMMITTING here, and it calls every participant of the chain, joined or not

origin.section: 15.3 Recovery Aborts What Was Preparing and Commits Again What Was Committing

questions.stem: A cinema server's chain is HoldSeat (holds a seat with an outside booking service in prepare, joins, releases the hold in abort), then CheckVoucher, then SendResponse. Its journal is in memory. CheckVoucher finds the voucher row locked and answers RETRY once; on the next attempt it votes PREPARED. When the purchase is approved, what has the booking service seen?

options.text: One hold, since the retry carries on with the same transaction from CheckVoucher
options.says: a retried Context starts as a new transaction, under a new id, from the first participant, so HoldSeat holds again

options.text: One hold, since HoldSeat's abort released the first hold before the retry
options.says: after RETRY nobody gets commit or abort, so the first hold is never released

options.text: Two holds, both confirmed, since each attempt commits what it prepared
options.says: the first attempt ends with neither commit nor abort; only the second attempt commits

options.text: Two holds, one never released, since nobody told HoldSeat how the first attempt ended
options.says: RETRY calls neither commit nor abort and the retry runs the chain again, so the first hold leaks

origin.section: 15.5 `RETRY` Starts Over Under a New Id, and Nobody Hears How the First Attempt Ended

questions.stem: A participant asks a sanctions-screening service and returns PAUSE | NO_JOIN | READONLY. 80 ms later the service's callback stores a pass and calls ctx.resume(). The next participant, a plain TransactionParticipant, builds the approval, and SendResponse comes last. What does the terminal receive?

options.text: The approval, since the next participant runs as soon as the callback resumes the transaction
options.says: the next participant runs only on the prepare path; this transaction resumes on the abort path

options.text: The approval, since READONLY tells the TransactionManager that the pause changed nothing
options.says: READONLY only skips a snapshot; the missing PREPARED bit makes the vote an abort

options.text: Nothing, since the resumed transaction goes on along the abort path and skips the next participant
options.says: a vote without PREPARED is an abort; after the resume only abort participants are asked, and no response was built

options.text: Nothing, since a paused transaction with no pause-timeout is never taken off the queue again
options.says: resume() puts the Context back in the queue (unit s4) and a session takes it, as the trail shows; pause-timeout is only a safety net

origin.section: 15.4 A Vote Is Read Bit by Bit, and Only `PREPARED` Says Yes

questions.stem: Inside a Join, CheckLimit votes PREPARED | NO_JOIN | READONLY and ReserveStock votes PREPARED. A participant after the Join declines the purchase. On jPOS 2.1.7, which call does CheckLimit get after its prepare?

options.text: None, since its NO_JOIN keeps it out of commit and abort as it would outside a Join
options.says: Join starts a fresh runner for every nested participant on abort, and a fresh runner remembers no vote

options.text: None, since only the Join itself joins the transaction and hears its outcome
options.says: the Join does hear the outcome, and it passes it on to every nested participant

options.text: An abort, since Join passes the outcome to each of its participants whatever it voted
options.says: in 2.1.7 Join calls abort on every nested participant, joined or not

options.text: A commit, since the Join as a whole had voted PREPARED before the decline
options.says: a later decline aborts the transaction, so the joined Join gets abort, not commit

origin.section: 15.7 `Join` Tells Every Nested Participant the Outcome, Joined or Not

concepts: A commit may run again after a crash and can journal nothing, so the outside call it makes must be safe to repeat.
Join runs its nested participants on new threads, without a timeout, and in 2.1.7 calls commit or abort on all of them whatever they voted.
A vote is read bit by bit: without PREPARED, a PAUSE or RETRY vote is an abort, and a paused transaction resumes on the abort path.
RETRY runs the transaction again under a new id from the first participant, with no commit or abort for the attempt, and a retry through a persistent journal loses the transient entries.
